questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 4(2)/(3) years at 6(3)/(4)% is Rs. 8,820. What will be the amount of the same sum after 7(1)/(2) years at 8(1)/(3) % at simple interest?
A sum of money lent out at simple interest amounts to Rs. 715 after 3 years and to Rs. 990 after a further period of 5 years. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 5 years = 990 − 715 = 275

Interest for 1 year = 275 ÷ 5 = 55

Interest for 3 years = 55 × 3 = 165

Principal (Sum) = Amount₃ yᵣₛ − Interest₃ yᵣₛ = 715 − 165 = 550

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** after 3 years (A₁) = Rs. 715

**Amount** after a further 5 years (total 8 years) (A₂) = Rs. 990

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da8fc46eb26fb2089c47771805f9bc131a55349257ab0d566a88a27862814407.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total duration for second amount = 3 + 5 = 8 years

⇒ Interest for (8 − 3) years = Rs. (990 − 715)

⇒ Interest for 5 years = Rs. 275

⇒ **Yearly Interest** = 275 ÷ 5 = Rs. 55

⇒ Interest for first 3 years = 55 × 3 = Rs. 165

⇒ Principal (Sum) = Amount after 3 years − Interest for 3 years

⇒ Principal = 715 − 165 = Rs. 550

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal** (P).

Amount Formula

The total **Amount** (A) is the sum of the principal and the interest earned over time T: A = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Rate Calculation

If required, the **Rate of Interest** (R) can be found using R = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T). For this problem, R = (55 × 100) ÷ (550 × 1) = 10%.</p

questions.question: An amount shall become 300% of the principal amount. When the rate is 10% per annum, then what is the time?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An amount shall become 300% of the principal amount.

Rate(R) = 10%

**Formula used:**

SI = PRT/100

P = Principal

A = Amount

**Calculation:**

Let, P = 100

∴ A = 300

Then,** SI = A - P**

SI = 300 - 100 = 200

⇒ 200 = 100 × 10 × T/100

10T = 200

**∴ T = 20 Years**

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 12% per annum is ₹60 less than the simple interest on the same sum for 3 years at 10% per annum. The sum (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Simple Interest** percentage for 1st case = 12% × 2 = 24%.

Effective **Simple Interest** percentage for 2nd case = 10% × 3 = 30%.

Difference in interest percentage = 30% − 24% = 6%.

Given that 6% of the **Sum** = ₹60.

∴ Total **Sum** (100%) = (60 ÷ 6) × 100 = ₹1,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate 1 (R₁) = 12%, Time 1 (T₁) = 2 years

Rate 2 (R₂) = 10%, Time 2 (T₂) = 3 years

Difference in **Simple Interest** = ₹60

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2060b1e0c854235ed16b4c611961e61a68881a3d8222f8ad78234a322eb39465.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Sum** be P.

⇒ SI₂ − SI₁ = 60

⇒ [(P × 10 × 3) ÷ 100] − [(P × 12 × 2) ÷ 100] = 60

⇒ (30P ÷ 100) − (24P ÷ 100) = 60

⇒ 6P ÷ 100 = 60

⇒ 6P = 6000

⇒ P = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Components

The **Principal** (P) is the initial sum, **Rate** (R) is the percentage interest per year, and **Time** (T) must always be in years for the standard formula SI = PRT/100.

Total Amount Formula

The total **Amount** (A) after T years is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Difference between SI and CI

For the first year, SI and **Compound Interest** (CI) are equal if the interest is compounded annually. For 2 years, the difference is P(R/100)².

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at a certain rate of simple interest. In how many years will it become four times of itself at the same rate of simple interest ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **Simple Interest**, use the formula: (n₁ − 1) / T₁ = (n₂ − 1) / T₂

Where n is the **multiplier** and T is the **time**.

⇒ (2 − 1) / 8 = (4 − 1) / T₂

⇒ 1 / 8 = 3 / T₂

⇒ T₂ = 8 × 3 = 24 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T₁) = 8 years

Amount (A₁) = 2 × Principal (P)

Target Amount (A₂) = 4 × Principal (P)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d45ec90908c6abb336fd13672d2a098b0290987292b2ace9f1472e0616aae8f9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest** (SI₁) = A₁ − P = 2P − P = P

⇒ This interest P is earned in 8 years.

⇒ For the sum to become 4 times, **Interest** (SI₂) = A₂ − P = 4P − P = 3P

⇒ In **Simple Interest**, the interest earned is directly proportional to time.

⇒ Time required (T₂) = (SI₂ / SI₁) × T₁

⇒ T₂ = (3P / P) × 8

⇒ T₂ = 3 × 8 = 24 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

The formula is SI = (P × R × T) / 100, where **P** is Principal, **R** is Rate per annum, and **T** is Time in years.

Rate of Interest Calculation

If a sum doubles in T years at SI, the rate **R** = 100 / T. In this case, R = 100 / 8 = 12.5%.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total **Amount (A)** is the sum of the Principal and the Interest earned: A = P + SI.

Proportionality Rule

In Simple Interest, the interest earned for any period is constant, meaning **Interest** is directly proportional to the **Time** duration.</p

questions.question: In what time does a sum of money amount to twice of itself at the simple interest of 25% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **n** times of itself at Simple Interest rate **R%**, the time **T** is given by:

T = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ R

Here, n = 2 (since it becomes twice) and R = 25%.

⇒ T = [(2 − 1) × 100] ÷ 25

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 years

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rate of Interest (R) = 25% per annum

Let the Principal (P) be 100 units.

Since the sum amounts to twice itself, Amount (A) = 2 × 100 = 200 units.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Amount − Principal

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Start (t = 0)
 End (t = ?)
 
 P = 100 units
 A = 200 units
 
 
 

 

 
 
 SI = +100 units
 Rate = 25% p.a.

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = 200 − 100 = 100 units

⇒ 100 = (100 × 25 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 25 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 25

⇒ T = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum becoming 'n' times (Rate Calculation)

If a sum becomes 'n' times of itself in 'T' years at simple interest, the rate can be found directly by: R = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ T.

Direct Amount Formula for SI

The total amount A after T years can be calculated as: A = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

Rule of 72

A general financial shortcut used to estimate the time required to double an investment when the interest is compounded: Time ≈ 72 ÷ R. However, for Simple Interest, the exact doubling time is always 100 ÷ R.
</p

questions.question: A man invests an amount of Rs. 1,05,750 at simple interest in the name of his son, daughter and his wife in such a way that they get the same interest after 3, 4 and 5 years, respectively. If the rate of interest is 5% per annum. then the amount invested for the wife is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total amount = Rs. 105750

Rate of interest = 5%

**Concept used:**

S.I = PTR/100

**Calculation:**

Let share of his son, daughter, wife be x, y, z

According to the question,

x × 3 × 5/100 = y × 4 × 5/100 = 5 × z × 5/100

⇒ 3x = 4y = 5z

LCM of 3, 4, 5 = 60

So, Ratio of x : y : z = 20 : 15 : 12

Now,

20 + 15 + 12 = 47

Here 47 = 105750

1 = 2250

12 = 27000

So, his wife got Rs. 27000

**∴ The amount invested for the wife is Rs. 27000**
